_note: Original advanced lesson. Language-specific code appears through block variants.
title: Recursion Patterns
summary: Solve a problem by handling a small case, then calling the same function on a smaller version.
refresher: A recursive function needs a base case that stops and a recursive call that moves closer to that stop. If the call does not shrink the problem, recursion can run forever.
refresher_code:
if base_case: return answer
return solve(smaller_input)

sections.title: Base case first
sections.summary: The base case is the stopping rule.

blocks.body: A base case handles the smallest version directly. For factorial, `0!` and `1!` are both 1, so the function can stop there.

blocks.caption: Each call uses a smaller n until it reaches the base case.

blocks.prompt: What is the job of the base case?
blocks.why: Without a base case, the function has no clear place to stop.

sections.title: Make the problem smaller
sections.summary: Every recursive call must move toward the base case.

blocks.body: The recursive call should not repeat the same input. If `factorial(n)` calls `factorial(n)` again, nothing changes and the program keeps calling itself.

blocks.caption: The call must move toward the stopping rule.

choices: n gets smaller until it reaches the base case
blocks.why: Each call gets closer to `n <= 1`, where the function returns without another call.
